title: Establish composable error patterns for grouped inputs and progressive disclosure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The design system currently has inconsistent error behavior across single inputs, grouped inputs (date ranges, address blocks, credit card forms), and multi-step/progressive forms. Developers are implementing ad-hoc patterns: sometimes an error banner is used, other times inline messages, and keyboard/screen-reader announcements vary. This ticket defines a composable, token-aligned error pattern that works for grouped inputs, summary/error lists, and progressive disclosure flows while meeting accessibility and density requirements.
acceptance_criteria: A documented error composition pattern exists in the design system page with visuals for single input, grouped inputs, and multi-step forms
Semantic tokens for error color/contrast mapped to role tokens (error-border, error-text, error-icon, error-bg) with recommended alpha values for light/dark themes
HTML/ARIA recommendations for error summary (role="alert" vs role="status") and keyboard focus behaviour across browsers documented
Design specs include mobile variants (stacked vs inline), spacing tokens to avoid content shift, and guidelines for truncation/ellipsis in error summary
Frontend team has an initial implementation PR that matches the design tokens and provides a Storybook with examples
QA checklist produced: keyboard nav, screen reader announcements, high-contrast mode, autofill error handling
design_notes: Favor one clear primary indication (color + icon) per field; use an aggregated error summary at the top for grouped inputs and multi-step forms
Introduce 'error-intent' semantic token group: error-strong, error-muted, error-bg-subtle. These must map to existing color tokens and pass 4.5:1 contrast for body text where applicable

For grouped inputs (eg. card expiry MM/YY or address line block), allow an outer-group error state that includes: outer border highlight, concise summary text below group, and per-field microcopy for granular feedback
Progressive disclosure flows (stepper) should show a compact banner on step change listing errors and should not auto-navigate away from focused field unless user chooses

Microcopy guidelines: prioritize actionable language ("Enter a valid expiry month") over generic labels ("Invalid input"). Provide examples for common validation patterns (email, expiry, card number, postal code)
Provide token spacing guidance to prevent layout shifts when inline errors appear; use reserved 20px vertical space on input variants where density allows
decisions: Use aggregated error summary for groups by default; per-field inline message only shown after user interaction (blur or attempted submit)
Use role="alert" for live region on form submit errors to ensure SR announcement; for inline errors use aria-describedby and aria-invalid on the input
Error color tokens will be new semantic tokens (error-strong, error-muted) that map to existing palette; do not introduce arbitrary hex values in components
Do not automatically scroll users when showing summary errors unless a clear visual focus target is moved to; instead provide a 'View errors' link that focuses the summary
open_questions: Should the group-level error message be clickable to jump to the first invalid field? (trade-off: focus management complexity)
How should we expose configurable behavior for teams that want immediate inline validation vs deferred validation? (proposal: prop on Form component: validationStrategy="deferred|immediate|onSubmit")
Do we need a separate 'warning' intent token set for non-blocking feedback? If so, how does it differ visually from error to avoid confusion?
tasks: Finalize semantic token names and publish mapping table for light/dark (Owner: Design)
Create Figma component variants: Single input error, Group outer error, Aggregated summary, Stepper banner (Owner: Design)
Write ARIA guidance and examples for screen reader behavior (Owner: Design + Accessibility engineer)
Implement Storybook stories + CSS variables using new tokens (Owner: Frontend)
QA run against Chrome, Safari, VoiceOver, NVDA and mobile browsers (Owner: QA)
Collect feedback from 3 product teams using grouped inputs (payments, onboarding, billing) and iterate (Owner: UX Research)
